reconcile.connective: Defenders distinguish two acts of writing: God re-engraved the Ten Words on the tablets, while Moses wrote out the surrounding covenant terms (or a copy).

discrepancy.connective: Source critic Richard Elliott Friedman reads Exodus 34:1 and 34:27-28 as a redactional seam: in the underlying J narrative Moses writes the tablets, and 34:1's "I will write" was added to splice this account to the God-written tablets of Exodus 32, leaving the two attributions unreconciled.

skeptic.name: Richard Elliott Friedman
skeptic.work: The Bible with Sources Revealed: A New View into the Five Books of Moses
skeptic.attribution: Richard Elliott Friedman, The Bible with Sources Revealed (HarperSanFrancisco, 2003), 177-179

excerpts.excerpt_text: But here, in Exo 34:27, it seems as if Moses was commanded to write these words, and in Exo 34:28 it is said, And he wrote upon the tables; but in Deu 10:1-4 it is expressly said that God wrote the second tables as well as the first. … This supposition removes the apparent contradiction; and thus both God and Moses may be said to have written the covenant and the ten commandments: the former, the original; the latter, the copy.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke names the exact tension (34:27-28 reads as Moses writing vs. Deut 10:1-4 stating God wrote) and offers the standard harmonization: God wrote the Ten Words; Moses wrote a copy/the other precepts, so both can be said to have written. Single strongest reconcile, parity-capped to the one named-skeptic discrepancy entry.

pd_work.resource: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832), note on Exodus 34:1
pd_work.author: Adam Clarke
pd_work.note: Clarke treats this passage directly, framing the apparent contradiction between Exodus 34:27-28 and Deuteronomy 10:1-4 and resolving it by distinguishing God's writing of the Ten Words from Moses' writing of a copy/the accompanying precepts. Used because Haley's specific-passage coverage could not be confirmed; Clarke is a harmonizing commentator already surfaced on this row and keyed to the passage.
